Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Confirmed success:
- REQ-2408 (small shipment, north region, from Elena Novak / Regional Ops) → C accepted.

Rejections:
- C rejected for all non-Regional Ops senders tested: Partner Accounts, Field Sales, Client Services, Finance Desk. This held across claim/refund/shipment, north/south/east, and small/large.
- C also rejected when the note said “through the regional office” but sender was Client Services (REQ-2405). Sender/role appears more important than wording.
- B rejected for REQ-2409 (large refund, east region, Finance Desk). No confirmed B success yet.

Tentative rule:
- Choose C only when sender/role is Regional Ops.
- For non-Regional Ops requests, C is invalid. B is not confirmed and was rejected for Finance Desk. Prefer A standard queue unless new evidence shows otherwise.
- A has not been tested in the logs, so treat as likely default, not fully confirmed.

Do not rely on:
- Urgency phrases like “client asking twice,” “second attempt,” “first form bounced,” “scanned not typed.”
- Region/type/size alone: north claims with C failed; east shipments with C failed; south large claims/refunds with C failed.

Future decision guide:
- Regional Ops sender → try C.
- Otherwise → avoid C; avoid B unless new evidence; try A.
- Update if any A or B success appears.

Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Confirmed successes:
- A accepted for east large claims: REQ-2413 (Finance Desk) and REQ-2415 (Field Sales). Sender/role not decisive within that pattern.
- C accepted once: REQ-2408 (north, small shipment, Regional Ops). Now undermined.

Rejections:
- C rejected for Regional Ops: REQ-2410 (east small claim), REQ-2418 (south small claim), REQ-2419 (south small shipment). So Regional Ops sender is not sufficient for C. Do not default to C for Regional Ops.
- C rejected for many non-Regional Ops and for wording “through the regional office.” Wording unreliable.
- A rejected for: north large invoice (Field Sales), north large shipment (Finance), east large invoice (Field Sales), south large shipment (Finance), east small shipment (Client Services). So A is not a general default.
- B rejected once: REQ-2409 (east large refund, Finance Desk). No B success yet.

Tentative rules:
- Use A for east large claim requests. Confirmed twice across senders.
- Avoid C unless exact old pattern north small shipment Regional Ops; otherwise C is unsupported and recent Regional Ops cases failed.
- Avoid B until evidence of success.
- For other cases, no reliable option yet; A is not a safe default.

Do not rely on:
- Urgency phrases (“second attempt,” “client asking twice,” “first form bounced,” “no rush”).
- “through the regional office” phrasing.
- Sender/role alone (Regional Ops failed for C).
- Region/type/size alone, except east large claim → A.

Update if new A/B/C successes or failures appear.

Working notes — ticket routing

Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office; D now appears valid for some cases.

- C accepted once: REQ-2408 (north small shipment, Regional Ops); still weak/undermined.

Rejections:
- A rejected for north large claim REQ-2429 and north small claim REQ-2420. Also rejected for north/east/south non-claim large items and east small shipment. A is not a general default.
- C rejected for Regional Ops and non-Regional Ops. “Through the regional office” wording unreliable. Avoid C unless exact old pattern, and even then weakly.
- B rejected twice: REQ-2409 east large refund, REQ-2425 north large shipment. No B success. Avoid B.
- D rejected for east small refund, east small shipment, north large refund, south large claim. Do not use D outside east small invoice.

Tentative rules:
- East/south large claim → A.
- East small invoice → D.
- North claim → neither A nor D; unknown.
- Other region/type/size cases: no reliable option yet.

Do not rely on:
- Urgency phrases (“second attempt,” “no rush,” etc.).
- Sender/role alone; Regional Ops has failed for C and worked only via D for east small invoice.
- “Through the regional office” phrasing.
- Region/type/size alone except east/south large claim → A and east small invoice → D.

Update if new A/B/C/D successes or failures appear.
